title: Intermittent Connectivity POC — Hosting & Fallback Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This playbook captures a lightweight, reproducible approach for customer POCs where the target environment has intermittent or constrained network connectivity (factory floors, maritime vessels, rural retail sites, air-gapped satellites). Goal: validate a hybrid hosting model that prioritizes correctness and availability while measuring cost and operational overhead for moving from hosted -> dedicated -> private (on-prem/VPC).

Context & constraints (customer brief):
- Limited egress windows (e.g., NAT timed access, satcom windows).
- Low bandwidth: typical sustained throughput 256–1,000 kbps, bursts tolerated during maintenance windows.
- Strict data residency: some telemetry must remain local; aggregate, anonymized metrics may be allowed through vetted channels.
- Hardware: 1–2x on-prem T4-class GPUs or equivalent CPU fallback.
- Workload: user-facing chat/assistant and short-form generation (<= 512 tokens), occasional batch reranks.

Decision criteria (what we measure in the POC):
- Availability SLA observed (p95 latency, 99th percentile success rate) when hosted is unreachable.
- Quality delta between hosted and local model variants (BLEU/ROUGE or domain-specific eval set).
- Cost of reserved capacity vs hosted egress + sync overhead.
- Operational complexity (#procedures, manual interventions per month).
- Privacy/compliance gap (data leaving site by design).

Recommended POC pattern (three phased topologies):
1) Primary-hosted with periodic delta-sync -> Local warm standby
   - Primary: Redwood hosted API (best-performing model) for normal ops.
   - Local: lightweight private runtime (quantized variant) deployed as a standby in the site network.
   - Sync model deltas and prompt templates during scheduled maintenance windows (rsync-like model artifact + small checksum manifest).
   - Local serves only when health-checks to hosted endpoints fail or when latency > configured threshold.
   - Advantages: lowest operational cost; keeps inference in hosted plane most of the time.
   - Risks: potential quality gap; requires reliable scheduled sync windows.

2) Dedicated-reserved with regional caching + local fallback
   - Primary: Dedicated pool in nearest region with predictable throughput.
   - Local cache: persistent KV-cache and prefix caching to accelerate local fallback.
   - Sync strategy: keep model weights in warm storage (compressed) and only pull to local GPU when sustained outage > X minutes.
   - Advantages: predictable latency when reachable; better quality parity.
   - Tradeoffs: higher committed cost; more complex routing.

3) Private-first (air-gapped) with controlled telemetry bridge
   - Primary runtime runs fully on-prem. Control plane optionally managed through an approved bridge.
   - Telemetry controlled by scheduled batched egress and on-site KMS for key protection.
   - Suitable when sovereignty/regulatory restrictions mandate no model calls off-site.

Fallback orchestration patterns (behavioral rules):
- Passive failover: local instance monitors health of hosted/dedicated endpoints every 10s; on 5 consecutive failures switch to local.
- Quality-aware fallback: instrument prompt/eval sampling; if local nudge falls below quality threshold for >N requests, service re-route to best available variant (might degrade to cached responses with disclaimer).
- Graceful degrade: when local model is serving low-confidence outputs, append a confidence tag and route sensitive flows to humans.

Sync & artifact management (practical notes):
- Artifact packaging: model.tar.gz with manifest.json (sha256s per file), tokenizer, and evaluation snippets. Keep artifacts < 2GB when possible.
- Delta sync: send only quantization tables + small weight deltas when network limited. Our proto supports block-delta transfers; verify compatibility.
- Transfer window: use rsync over TLS or SFTP; schedule during known off-hours. Retries exponential backoff (cap 8 attempts).
- Versioning: semantic model version + build id (e.g., v1.3.0-20251104). Local runtime must validate manifest and fail safe to earlier local version if checksum mismatch.

KV/prefix cache guidance for intermittent sites:
- Persist KV cache to SSD with LRU eviction. Target local cache 8–16GB for common contexts.
- TTLs: conservative 24–48h for prompt prefixes; shorter for user PII-containing entries (rotate to null).
- Warmup: prefetch top 500 prompt prefixes during sync window.

Model selection & quantization guidance:
- Host uses full FP16 or bfloat variant. Local fallback uses 4-bit or 8-bit quantized variant chosen by quality tests.
- Evaluate logits-level divergence on a 200-sample domain set; accept quantized variant if top-1 token agreement >= 92% and task-specific metric drop <= 3%.

Security & compliance checklist:
- KMS: local keys stored in HSM/KMS or customer-managed solution. Keys rotated quarterly.
- Audit logs: local audit collector aggregates logs and shares digests only (no PII).
- Egress policy: all outbound allowed only to preapproved Redwood endpoints; firewall rules documented.
- Consent & legal: ensure data-handling agreement covers occasional telemetry egress and model updates.

Testing matrix (minimum tests to include in POC):
- Connectivity simulation: captive failure for 5s, 30s, 10m, 2h. Observe failover time and correctness.
- Throughput ramp: 1->50 concurrent requests over 10 minutes; measure tails.
- Model parity: run 200 domain prompts comparing hosted vs local variant, capture metrics.
- Sync robustness: interrupt transfers at multiple points and validate resume.
- Cold restart: reboot local node and assert automated recover to previous local model within N minutes.

SLO targets (POC baseline):
- P95 latency (local fallback, < 128 tokens): < 350ms on GPU, < 1.2s on CPU fallback.
- Failover detection: 95% of decisions complete within 12s of outage window.
- Model quality retention: local variant quality >= 90% of hosted baseline on task metric.

Operational runbook (quick steps for site operators):
- Normal ops: monitor Redwood Console dashboard; accept scheduled syncs from 02:00–03:00 local.
- Host unreachable: local agent will log event, attempt health-check to alternate region; on 5 failed checks, start local runtime (if not already running).
- Model update failure: agent rolls back to prior manifest and sends alert to ops channel.
- Emergency: escalate to Redwood Solutions on-call and provide logs bundle (see linked_artifacts).

POC measurements & artifacts to collect:
- Health-check logs, failover timestamps, request traces (no PII), model diffs, sync metrics (bytes transferred, retries), cost burn-rate estimate for hosted vs local.
- Keep an artifacts folder with manifests, evaluation outputs, and a short README describing how to reproduce the sync.

Cost model template (simple):
- Hosted cost estimate = (avg tokens/day * hosted price/token) + egress during sync windows.
- Local cost estimate = reserved capacity amortized per month + storage + ops time.
- Breakeven analysis: compute monthly tokens at which dedicated/local is cheaper than hosted + intermittent egress.

Risks & mitigations quick list:
- Sync corruption -> use atomic swap and manifest checksums.
- Model drift -> schedule weekly evals against golden dataset and alert when drop > threshold.
- Unforeseen long outages -> provide degraded canned responses + user messaging.

Open questions for customer (to resolve during scoping call):
- Acceptable telemetry subset and retention rules?
- Maximum single artifact size we can push during maintenance window?
- Who on-site can perform physical restart or approve HSM access?
- Expected peak concurrency per site and number of sites for scale estimate.

Next steps & owners:
- Run initial connectivity simulation (Avery) by 2026-03-10.
- Assemble 200-sample domain eval (Priya) by 2026-02-14.
- Draft security boundary doc for customer review (Maya) by 2026-03-02.

Appendix: quick checklist for POC kickoff:
- [ ] Confirm sync window and bandwidth numbers.
- [ ] Cust signs telemetry/data handling addendum.
- [ ] Local hardware validated (GPU health, disk space).
- [ ] Gatekeeper credentials for secure transfer provisioned.
- [ ] Eval suite and success criteria finalized.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep first POC conservative: prefer hosted for quality while proving robust failover.
- If customer cares a lot about TCO, run the dedicated breakeven quickly — cost often surprises them when multiplied across many sites.
- We should template a small rsync + verify script to include in the onboarding bundle.

End of playbook.
